questions.text: Which sea animal has three hearts?
questions.hint: It lives on the seafloor and has eight arms. Check the Sea life tab.
questions.why: The giant Pacific octopus has three hearts: two pump blood through its gills and one sends it around the body. Its blood is blue, too!

questions.text: Why is the water less salty near Tsawwassen?
options: A big river pours in fresh water
questions.hint: Look at the Seafloor tab near the end of the route.
questions.why: The Fraser River empties into the Strait of Georgia. Its fresh water is lighter than salt water, so it spreads out on top.

questions.text: What makes the tide go up and down?
options: The Moon pulling on the sea
questions.hint: The answer is in the sky. Check the Tides & weather tab.
questions.why: The Moon's gravity pulls the ocean into a bulge. As Earth spins through it, the water here rises and falls about twice a day.

questions.text: What do the orcas that live here mostly eat?
questions.hint: It is a big fish that swims up rivers to lay its eggs.
questions.why: Resident orcas in these waters mostly eat salmon, especially big Chinook salmon.

questions.text: What are the tiny plants that float in the sea called?
questions.hint: The ferry measures them with its chlorophyll sensor.
questions.why: Phytoplankton are tiny plant-like living things. They feed almost everything else in the sea, and the ferry measures them as chlorophyll.
